item.title: MSCA COFUND 2027
item.description: This call funds new or existing doctoral programmes with an impact on human resources in R&I at regional, national or international level, co-funded by MSCA COFUND. The aim is to provide doctoral candidates with diverse research and transferable skills, improving employability and career prospects. Legal entities established in EU Member States or Associated Countries can apply to set up these programmes, which must offer research training leading to a doctoral degree. Programme: Horizon Europe – HORIZON TMA MSCA Cofund Doctoral programme. Eligible countries: EU Member States and associated countries. Who can lead: Applicants submit proposals for new or existing doctoral programmes.. Deadline: 6 Apr 2027. item.title: Early-Stage Innovative Technology Development for Basic and Clinical Cancer Research (R61 Clinical Trial Not Allowed)
item.description: The National Cancer Institute solicits grant applications proposing to develop innovative technologies for cancer research or clinical care. The emphasis is on early-stage projects proposing proof-of-concept or pilot studies to test the technical feasibility of proposed methods, tools, assays, platforms, or instruments. Eligible applicants include domestic and foreign non-profit and for-profit organizations, public and private institutions of higher education, governments, and small businesses. item.title: Leveraging functional genomics to reveal novel targets for cancer treatment
item.description: This call funds research and innovation actions aimed at leveraging functional genomics to understand tumour heterogeneity, discover next-generation cancer treatments, and contribute to the UNCAN.eu research data platform. Proposals should focus on paediatric, rare, and refractory cancers, using exploratory mechanistic studies and clinical proof-of-concept. Eligible applicants include consortia of researchers, health professionals, and innovators from EU Member States and associated countries. Programme: Horizon Europe – HORIZON Research and Innovation Actions. Eligible countries: EU Member States and associated countries. Deadline: 16 Sep 2027. Official call: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/topic-details/HORIZON-MISS-2027-02-CANCER-01

item.description: The Scientist Development Award supports early-career rheumatologists and health professionals in launching independent research careers by funding salary and research expenses under the guidance of a mentor. Eligible applicants include post-doctoral researchers, fellows, and physicians affiliated with accredited academic institutions who dedicate at least 75 percent of their effort to research. item.title: Empowering Lupus Research Partnership NOSI FY 2028
item.description: This funding initiative, resulting from a collaboration between the Lupus Research Alliance and the Rheumatology Research Foundation, supports translational and clinical research focused on systemic lupus erythematosus and related autoimmune conditions. It aims to develop innovative diagnostic and therapeutic strategies by leveraging clinical data and patient stratification. Two funding pathways are available: the Scientist Development Award for early-career researchers and the Investigator Award. Grants provide up to 225,000 USD for a maximum duration of three years. Programme: LRARRF Empowering Lupus Research Partnership NOSI FY 2028. Eligible countries: Not stated in the official text: check the call. Deadline: see the official call. item.description: This funding opportunity supports the translation of genome editing and other biologic therapies for Alzheimer's Disease-Related Dementias across the full translational pipeline, from therapeutic lead optimization and drug product development through IND-enabling studies and early clinical evaluation. item.description: The Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation offers master's scholarships for nationals of PALOP countries to pursue master's degrees in mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology at Portuguese higher education institutions. The funding covers a monthly stipend, relocation expenses, tuition fee support, and travel allowances. item.description: The Gulbenkian Integration Initiative supports civil society projects that promote the integration of immigrants and involve host communities in Portugal. It funds innovative, participatory approaches addressing language learning, employment, housing, healthcare, and education. item.description: This funding opportunity solicits applications to create a national network of Children's Environmental Health Research Translation Centers. The centers aim to protect and improve children's health by developing and testing new scientific questions and public health interventions, translating research findings for the wider community, and mentoring new investigators interested in translational children's environmental health. item.description: This Notice of Funding Opportunity solicits phased UG3/UH3 cooperative agreement applications for investigator-initiated interventional clinical trials addressing rheumatic, musculoskeletal, or skin diseases and disorders. item.title: Advancing Real-World Effectiveness Evidence for Rapid-Acting Psychotropic Interventional Drugs (RAPIDs)
item.description: This funding opportunity encourages applications to establish a Rapid-Acting Psychotropic Interventional Drugs Clinical Trials Network. The aim is to generate actionable, real-world evidence to guide the safe and effective implementation of rapid-acting psychotropics in routine clinical practice. The program funds milestone-driven, large-scale coordinated network projects structured into two operational stages for network establishment, pilot studies, and full-scale pragmatic trials. Eligible applicants include various governmental, tribal, educational, nonprofit, and business organizations. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. item.description: The National Institute of Mental Health encourages applications for Silvio O. Conte Centers to support integrative research teams addressing high-risk, high-impact questions in basic neuroscience and translational mental health. item.title: NCI Research Specialist (Clinician Scientist) Award (R50)
item.description: This National Cancer Institute funding opportunity invites applications for the Research Specialist Award to support exceptional clinician scientists participating in NCI-funded clinical trials networks. Eligible applicants include various U.S. institutional types. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). item.title: Quarterly Research Grant Funding Programme
item.description: This programme funds preclinical and clinical research focused on slowing, stopping, or reversing Parkinson’s disease. It supports research conducted by industry and academia, either alone or in collaboration. Eligible projects include preclinical research up to £300,000, clinical infrastructure projects, and clinical trials. item.description: This funding opportunity supports the continuation of the Immune Tolerance Network to develop tolerogenic therapies for immune-mediated disorders. item.title: Parkinson's Disease Biomarker Innovation and Advancement Program
item.description: The Parkinson's Disease Biomarker Innovation and Advancement Program accelerates the development and validation of robust, fit-for-purpose measurement tools based on fluid- and imaging-based biomarkers for Parkinson's disease. The program funds biotechnology, biopharma, diagnostic, and imaging companies, contract research organizations (CROs), and select academic-industry partnerships. Projects must have a clear path to commercialization and broader research community access. A two-stage rolling application process is used, starting with a continuous pre-proposal submission followed by invited full proposals. item.description: This call by NordForsk, with Forte as a partner, aims to strengthen and support high-quality transdisciplinary research on women's health within the Nordic-Baltic region. item.title: Visitor Training Program
item.description: The Visitor Training Program provides funding for hematologists and healthcare professionals in low- and middle-income countries to receive up to 12 weeks of training on specific hematology topics or techniques in the clinic or laboratory of an ASH member. The program covers visa fees, airfare, accommodations, and daily living expenses. item.description: The ASH Quality Improvement Training Institute (QITI) is a 12-month hybrid educational program that pairs interdisciplinary healthcare teams with quality improvement coaches to execute projects addressing clinical gaps in hematology care.
